title: Lipschitz Boolean-to-Gaussian invariance bound
statement:
There exists a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds for all natural numbers $n,d$, all functions $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ whose Walsh coefficients vanish on sets of size greater than $d$, and all $\varepsilon\ge0$: if $\operatorname{Var}(f)\le1$ and every coordinate influence satisfies $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\le\varepsilon$, then for every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)}\psi(f(x))-\mathbb E_{z\sim\gamma^{\otimes n}}\psi\!\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}z_i\right)\right|\le Kc\,2^d\varepsilon^{1/4},
\]
where $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian law on $\mathbb R$ and $\widehat f(S)$ are the Walsh coefficients of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
The Walsh coefficients of $f$ vanish on every set of size greater than $d$
The variance of $f$ is at most one
Every coordinate influence of $f$ is at most $\varepsilon$
